defensibility_rule: A rank-1 method is 'partly' defensible only when its own documentation states an obligation that the trigger input observably violates, even though its body contains no faulty statement and the omitted logic lives elsewhere; it is 'no' when its only claim is being called by the test, lying on the call path, or being the method that forms the output, while its documentation is silent on the violated property; 'yes' would require the rank-1 body itself to contain the omission. Applied to B4: StatUtils.mode carries the only 'NaN values are ignored' promise on the path (javadoc lines 808 and 834), returns NaN on the trigger, and the pre-variant code kept the isNaN guard inside StatUtils' own private helper (visible in the removed hunk of variant.patch), so a careful engineer could place a pre-delegation filter there, but its body is a null check plus a one-line delegation (both overloads), and the guard the variant dropped is in FastMath.tabulate's loop; hence every facade-rank-1 run (7C06F2/run-004, 7C06F2/run-005, CCA96B/run-001, CCA96B/run-004, CCA96B/run-005) is 'partly', uniformly, regardless of whether the chain located the divergence. MathArrays.mostFrequent (7C06F2/run-003) documents only 'most frequently occurring value(s) ... in ascending order', which [NaN] literally satisfies, and no in-method filter can recover [0, 2] once NaN has out-counted 0 and 2 in the Frequency table, so it is 'no'.
